answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The mechanism therefore aligns self-interest with network health: an attacker gains most by behaving honestly, because that is the only move that scales.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a trellis as the anchor of the cost.
